android.desc: TapLock lets you easily add a transparent, resizable widget to your home screen for one-touch phone locking with a simple double-tap! Upgraded to a new phone only to find that the double-tap-to-lock feature is missing? I was frustrated too! TapLock solves that by allowing you to lock your phone instantly without pressing the power button. Key Features: 🥞 Simple Setup: Long-press an empty space on your home screen, then add the TapLock widget to get started. 🪛 Instant Locking: Double-tap the widget to lock your phone instantly. 📏 Resizable Widget: Customize the widget's size to perfectly fit your screen. 🔒 Privacy-Focused: No personal information collected, and no data is accessed—your privacy is our priority! ⚡Please note⚡ Accessibility permission are required for TapLock to detect your double-tap gesture and lock your phone. You can easily enable this permission within the app. For complete transparency, the source code is available at https://github.com/modelorona/TapLock Privacy policy is available at https://anguelh.com/privacy_policies/taplock

quotes.text:
When I switched from a Samsung to a Pixel, I was shocked to discover that the 'double-tap to lock' feature (where you double-tap an empty area of the home screen to lock your device) wasn't a native option.

This feature existed as far back as 2014 on my LG G3, so why is it missing on the Pixel?

While there are alternatives on the Play Store, most are either closed-source or bundled into custom launchers — neither of which I wanted. Sending the lock-screen signal requires the Accessibility Service, and I wasn’t comfortable granting that level of access to a closed-source third-party app.

So, I decided to create my own solution. My app is completely open-source, contains no tracking or analytics libraries, and doesn’t make any external requests. The Accessibility Service permission is used solely to send the lock-screen command. I tried to find an alternative to locking the screen without requiring Accessibility permissions but the options either required root or weren't what I needed.

I also saw this as a chance to explore modern Android development. The last time I built an app from scratch, Jetpack Compose didn’t even exist. While I didn’t hate the experience, I won’t say I miss the days of wrestling with XML either. That said, some aspects of Compose felt harder to fully grasp and work with.

You can download it here: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.ah.taplock

Source code is here: https://github.com/modelorona/TapLock
